PullRequest.Title: sessions: wire cloud automations behind an experiment gate

## Summary

Wave 3 of the cloud automations stack, targeting `bevillal/cloud-automations-store` (#339407), not `main`. Rebuilt on wave2 commit `204512ca747`, which now uses the shared GitHub API domains from #339438 rather than the former provider-local API client.

- Extend `GitHubCloudAutomationStore` with serialized mutations and bounded run-history reads through leased shared GitHub clients, preserving repository eligibility, account/grant isolation, cancellation, and uncertain-write reconciliation.
- Add `CloudAutomationStore`, owned by the default Copilot sessions provider, to adapt definitions and runs to shared Automation contracts and manage account/feature lifecycle.
- Route operations to the owning provider behind `chat.automations.cloud.enabled`: default false, MACHINE scope, experimental/advanced, automatic treatment `config.chat.automations.cloud.enabled`, with parent Automations and AI-disable/visibility gates honored.
- Preserve UTC/custom schedules and acknowledgement-only dispatch results without inventing a native run or session. Keep existing consumers compatible with those shared contracts.
- Keep definition actions available when only history refresh fails; log unsupported task states and hide only their shared run projections while retaining raw history; reject unsupported null configuration resets.

The rebuilt stack keeps coordination and routing in separate commits: `4faeea15e6a` and `2cdf08d1569`.

## Scope and deferred work

User-owned definitions in known/recent private/internal GitHub.com repositories only; no account-wide scan or public/repository-owned automations.

Enabling the feature fetches definitions and exposes them to the existing card list. Cloud creation/edit dialogs and pickers, user-facing refresh/recovery, external-run history display/navigation, native-session adoption, and full cloud tool support remain deferred to later PRs. This is a default-off backend integration, not the complete cloud UX.

Existing tool changes are limited to excluding disabled stores and reporting accepted dispatches; they do not add cloud schedule configuration or refresh workflows. Unsupported custom triggers remain non-editable, and incompatible local-time blueprint/Agent Host conversions are rejected.

## Validation

Validated the rebuilt head `2cdf08d1569` with the updated base's locked dependencies:

- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- `npm run transpile-client` — passed.
- `scripts\test.bat --runGlob '**/{githubCloudAutomationStore,cloudAutomationStore,copilotChatSessionsProvider,providerAutomationService,automationRunner,automationTools,automations.contribution,automationDialog,automationBlueprint,automationService,agentHostAutomationStore,automationsView}.test.js'` — **490 passed, 4 pending**.
- `scripts\test.bat --runGlob '**/githubCloudDomains.test.js'` — **96 passed**.
- ESLint on all 24 changed TypeScript files — passed (`$files = git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACMR | Where-Object { $_.EndsWith('.ts') } | ForEach-Object { $_.Replace('/', '\') }; & .\node_modules\.bin\eslint.cmd $files`, run before committing).
- `npm run valid-layers-check` — passed.
- `git diff --cached --check` and both commit hygiene hooks — passed.

Coverage includes account/grant cancellation, client-lease cleanup, incomplete catalogue handling, mutation uncertainty, bounded history reads, accepted dispatches, unknown-state projection, and the existing provider/routing consumers. No live cloud mutation or UI end-to-end validation was run for this rebuild; changed-line coverage was not measured.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The queue identity, ordering, ready-state transition, automatic initial call path, network cardinality, and four-way limiter are all explicit in changed code and tests. Exact request duration and typical catalogue size vary, which affects severity but not the blocking mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: GitHub network requests queued ahead of user-triggered mutation requests
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The blocking work grows with the effective cloud catalogue: one listRuns request for every loaded definition, plus one tasks.get request for each active task among up to 50 returned runs per definition; only four definitions progress concurrently.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Run/Create/Update/Delete can remain queued for seconds or longer after the UI already reports the catalogue ready, making user actions appear hung and reducing mutation throughput.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this change the provider-local store only refreshed definitions and had neither automatic history hydration nor a shared FIFO that could place history reads ahead of mutations.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: CloudAutomationStore now starts refreshHistory immediately after definition refresh, while refreshHistory and every mutation both queue on the same Sequencer. Definition refresh publishes `ready` before history starts, so controls become enabled even though the full history fan-out is already ahead of subsequent user work.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 219 places the new history refresh on `this.operations`; added line 257 places mutations on the identical sequencer, and added lines 228-235 perform the scaling network fan-out before that queue item completes.
Findings.Title: Keep history hydration out of the mutation FIFO
Findings.Impact: With a realistic account containing multiple cloud automations, enabling the feature or rotating the account/client enables the cards and then issues per-definition history reads. A user clicking Run or editing a card during that period waits behind all of those reads; the added test demonstrates 10 definitions with four long-lived detail reads occupying the limiter.
Findings.Evidence: `CloudAutomationStore.refresh` awaits definition refresh and then calls `store.refreshHistory()` (cloudAutomationStore.ts:95-109). `refreshRepositories` sets catalogue state to `ready` before returning (githubCloudAutomationStore.ts:338-344). This changed line queues history on `operations`; lines 225-235 fan out `listRuns` and active-task `tasks.get` calls, while `mutate` at lines 257-273 queues Run/Create/Update/Delete on that same FIFO. The test at githubCloudAutomationStore.test.ts:304-319 creates 10 definitions and verifies four blocked detail requests, establishing both reachability and concurrency.
Findings.Recommendation: Use a separate cancellable/coalesced history-read lane, or otherwise prioritize admitted mutations, while publishing history only if its captured catalogue/account generation is still current. Keep definition refresh and writes serialized where ordering requires it, but do not make user mutations wait for the whole history window.

Scenarios.Scenario: Enable cloud automations, or rotate the default account/GitHub client, and load the cloud catalogue/history
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The adapter starts refresh asynchronously, so application startup itself does not await it. Definition discovery is on the cloud-card readiness path; history is on the history-section completion path and is started immediately after definitions publish ready.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve each local recent workspace through its Git configuration to a GitHub repository URI
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most 10 Agents-owned recent workspaces, processed sequentially; remote GitHub workspace URIs skip this boundary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The resolver existed for other provider work but was not wired into an automatically refreshed cloud automation adapter.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks definition discovery for later repositories because recent resolution is sequential, but does not block overall application startup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check repository visibility, list definition pages, and hydrate each definition detail
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per effective unique repository: one visibility request, up to 10 list pages of 100 summaries, and one detail request per definition in batches of 5. Repositories are the deduplicated union of up to 10 recents and all remembered eligible repositories.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The low-level explicit refresh path pre-existed, but this PR's adapter invokes it automatically when the enabled account/client lifetime is created.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All repositories are processed serially before cloud catalogue refresh completes and state settles ready/error.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List up to 50 runs per definition and fetch authoritative detail for every active run
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One listRuns request per loaded definition plus one tasks.get per queued/running/waiting task in each 50-run window; at most four definitions execute concurrently.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Does not delay definition state becoming ready, but occupies the shared operations FIFO before subsequent user mutations and delays history publication until all definitions finish.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective unique remembered/recent repositories R, loaded definitions D, and active tasks T; network work is approximately repository discovery plus D history-list calls plus T detail calls.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Recent resolution and repositories are serial. Definition details use batches of 5 per repository. History limits active definition jobs to 4, with task details serial inside each job. All refreshes, history reads, and mutations share one Sequencer.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Repository references persist per account and are deduplicated case-insensitively; definitions/history are memory-only and cold after account/client/gate transitions. A client lease is reused within one store lifetime. Concurrent definition refreshes coalesce via refreshPromise; history refreshes have no analogous coalescing promise.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: automatic invocation, exact request loops, cache lifetime, and concurrency are explicit in changed code and tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The feature defaults off and exact repository/definition/task counts and network latency vary. Remembered repositories can outlive the 10-item recent list, so larger long-lived catalogues remain realistic.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable because the introduced history fan-out uses the mutation FIFO after catalogue readiness, delaying interactive operations.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run, create, update, delete, or stop a cloud automation after the catalogue reports ready
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The user operation must enter the store's global Sequencer, revalidate repository visibility, then perform the requested remote mutation. During initial/account refresh it first waits for the already-queued complete history hydration.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Revalidate private repository eligibility and dispatch the requested automation/task mutation
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally two network operations per mutation: one getRepository eligibility read and one create/get+update/delete/dispatch/abort path; update uses preflight get and may therefore use three.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Cloud mutations were not implemented, and no history read could queue ahead of them.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Directly blocks the user's operation; additionally waits behind every earlier history request because both use the same FIFO.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Mutation latency scales with the queued history window D + T, then with its own two or three network round trips.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Global serialization: one definition refresh, history refresh, or mutation executes at a time at the outer Sequencer level; history internally fans out four definition jobs.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The GitHub client/credential lease is reused, but repository eligibility is deliberately re-read for every mutation. Indeterminate writes are negatively gated until a successful definition refresh reconciles state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: ready-state ordering and shared FIFO identity are explicit, and the test demonstrates long-lived history detail requests at the configured concurrency.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Users may not act immediately after enablement, but the UI publishes ready before history completes, making the overlap reachable; network duration varies.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable interactive latency regression; history should use a separate generation-checked/coalesced read lane or permit mutation priority.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render and observe the combined automation cards and run history
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Observable projections map cloud entries/runs, the provider aggregate flattens and sorts them, and the Automations view synchronously renders cards/history after each published snapshot.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Loaded definitions A and projected runs R, with cloud history capped at 50 runs per definition for one refresh window.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous observable recomputation/rendering on snapshot publication; no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network boundary occurs in this rendering path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Derived observables cache while observed; cloud snapshots replace arrays atomically. Unsupported states are filtered during projection.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the synchronous mapping/sorting path; low for material user-visible cost at realistic cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very large remembered catalogues could produce substantial arrays, but no changed per-frame/event loop or measured rendering mechanism establishes a separate high-confidence regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the changed projection work is snapshot-driven and the diff does not prove a distinct hot rendering regression.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 26 changed files and paginated large diffs. One medium-confidence-severity finding was submitted for per-definition history network fan-out blocking interactive cloud mutations through a shared FIFO. Automatic discovery, cache lifetimes, concurrency bounds, cancellation/disposal, aggregate rendering, and all transitive filesystem/network boundaries were also checked; no regression-fix learning signal was warranted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
